Vladimir Petkovic
62 Yrs  ·  Since Feb 2024
Petkovic came through the coaching ranks in Switzerland, having moved from the former Yugoslavia, and made his name at Bellinzona and Young Boys. He had a successful seven-year spell as Switzerland national head coach but less fortune at club level with Lazio and Bordeaux. He guided Algeria convincingly through World Cup qualifying and to the AFCON last eight, in a role where the pressure can sometimes be suffocating.
Tactics till May 2026
Algeria's shape places Zidane in goal behind Belghali, Mandi, Bensebaini and Ait-Nouri, with Boudaoui and Aouar in central midfield, Maza and Mahrez as the wide options and Gouiri and Amoura in attack. The goalkeeper spot is the most acute problem in the squad — Guendouz was first choice before injury, Luca Zidane unconvincing and then sidelined with a fractured jaw, and next in line Melvin Mastil plays in the Swiss second tier. In attack, 20-year-old Ibrahim Maza is already the creative pivot, while Mahrez is expected to keep his right-wing place in what will be his farewell tournament.

Lionel Scaloni
47 Yrs  ·  Since Aug 2018
Scaloni stands alongside Cesar Luis Menotti and Carlos Bilardo as Argentina World Cup-winning managers, having also won two Copas America and the 2022 Finalissima with sides that entertained and took the initiative. It is a remarkable achievement given he had no previous experience as head coach when brought in as interim after Argentina's dismal 2018 showing. Quiet and unassuming, he has also laid a blueprint for how Argentina continue when Messi finally retires.
Tactics till May 2026
Argentina's shape is a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, built around turning over possession and playing one-touch football with swift movement and clinical finishing. E. Martinez starts in goal behind Molina, Romero, Otamendi and Tagliafico, with De Paul, Fernandez and Mac Allister in midfield, Almada and Alvarez wide, and Messi at the ten. The midfield triumvirate of De Paul, Fernandez and Mac Allister is the engine supplying Messi while protecting a backline that has faced scrutiny. The two unsolved questions are how and when to deploy an ageing Messi, and who fills Di Maria's role — Almada is the leading candidate but the position remains unresolved.

Tony Popovic
52 Yrs  ·  Since Sep 2024
A popular former Socceroo who represented Australia at the 2006 World Cup, Popovic answered the call when Graham Arnold stepped down. He quickly established a new era of defensive stability, though questions remain over his ability to unlock Australia's attack. His insistence that players must be desperate to represent the jersey brought controversy when two youngsters, Triantis and Segecic, switched allegiance to Greece and Croatia despite earning call-ups under him.
Tactics till May 2026
Popovic favours a defensive 3-4-2-1 or 5-4-1 built around solidity at the back, with Ryan in goal behind Burgess, Souttar and Circati, though Souttar is returning from over a year out injured. Italiano and Bos operate as the wing-backs, with Irvine and O'Neill the likely midfield partnership, though several alternatives including Metcalfe, Balard and Yazbek are in contention. McGree and Irankunda provide the creative link ahead of them. The biggest unresolved question is who leads the line — Mohamed Toure was the frontrunner before injury, leaving Mitch Duke as the likely starter, with Irankunda and the wider attacking options expected to provide the cutting edge.

Ralf Rangnick
67 Yrs  ·  Since Jun 2022
Rangnick is one of the chief architects of Gegenpressing, whose coaching style inspired rivals including Nagelsmann and Tuchel. His German Cup win and Champions League semi-final with Schalke are footnotes compared to masterminding the rise of Hoffenheim and revolutionising football within the Red Bull network. Taking over a tame and lacklustre Austria in 2022, he has restored the attacking spark and earned the nation a first World Cup appearance.
Tactics till May 2026
Austria aim to win the ball high up the pitch and shoot away within seconds, consistent with Rangnick's Gegenpressing identity. A. Schlager starts in goal behind Laimer, Lienhart, Alaba and Mwene, with Seiwald and X. Schlager anchoring midfield, Baumgartner and Chukwuemeka providing creativity, and Sabitzer and Arnautovic leading the attack. Alaba brings big-game experience to the heart of defence if fit, while Laimer's ability to carry forward from full-back is Austria's key attacking outlet. The team is light on out-and-out striking options — Arnautovic and Gregoritsch are the primary choices, though neither is a conventional starter.

Rudi Garcia
62 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2025
A French club coach who won the Ligue 1 title with Lille in 2010-11 and had spells at Roma, Marseille, Lyon and Al Nassr. In his first national role he kept Belgium in UEFA Nations League A and clinched World Cup qualification, though he received little credit for either. His predecessor Tedesco fell to the pressures of Euro 2024, which should serve as a warning — Garcia also has no prior major international tournament experience.
Tactics till May 2026
Garcia's primary formation is a 4-3-3, which can shift into a 4-2-3-1, though a persistent injury list has prevented him from settling on a preferred XI or developing a distinctive style. Courtois starts in goal behind De Cuyper, Mechele, Debast and Meunier, with Onana and Tielemans in midfield and De Bruyne as the playmaking fulcrum ahead of them. Doku, Trossard and Lukaku complete the front line, with De Ketelaere as cover. De Bruyne's form after an injury-riddled season is a real concern, and Lukaku — Belgium's all-time top scorer — is recovering from a thigh and then hip injury with very little game time, making De Ketelaere the likely starter up front. Defence remains the persistent structural weakness.

Sergej Barbarez
54 Yrs  ·  Since Apr 2024
Legendary Bosnian captain who never reached a major tournament as a player, Barbarez carried that ambition into management after a career across Germany and Hamburg, then a spell playing professional poker. Taking charge mid-crisis — no wins in eight, a 7-0 loss to Germany — he rebuilt around diaspora talent, instilling energy and discipline. Within a year Bosnia went from broken to reborn.
Tactics till May 2026
Bosnia set up primarily in a 4-4-2 with two defensive midfielders, switching to a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3 when chasing games, with crosses into the box the preferred route back into matches. Vasilj starts in goal behind a back four of Dedic, Katic, Muharemovic and Kolasinac, with Tahirovic and Sunjic providing the midfield platform. Alajbegovic and Bajraktarevic operate as the wide outlets, driving fast transitions, while Dzeko leads the line. The system is heavily built around Dzeko's availability, and the two young wide players, though exciting, are raw enough to be considered a vulnerability as much as a strength.

Carlo Ancelotti
66 Yrs  ·  Since May 2025
Five Champions League titles across Europe's biggest clubs have made "Don Carlo" easy to underestimate as a World Cup coach, despite playing for Italy in 1986 and 1990 and later serving as assistant. A gum-chewing, eyebrow-raising figure whose low-profile, simplifying leadership style may suit the international game better than detail-obsessed club coaches. His legacy depends on delivering with Brazil.
Tactics till May 2026
Ancelotti's primary shape is a 4-2-4, with Casemiro recalled to anchor midfield alongside Bruno Guimaraes, a 4-3-3 a possible alternative. Alisson starts in goal behind a back four of Danilo, Marquinhos, Gabriel and Alex Sandro. Vinicius Junior and Raphinha provide wide threat, with Matheus Cunha operating as a hybrid No.9/No.10 and Estevao offering additional attacking danger. First-choice right-back Militao is out injured, leaving that position unresolved, while Estevao's fitness remains uncertain. Sustaining a two-man midfield through intense tournament heat is the tactical question Ancelotti has yet to fully answer.

Jesse Marsch
52 Yrs  ·  Since May 2024
American former Princeton graduate, Marsch brought cerebral, thoughtful football to Canada after their Qatar disappointment. In his first national role he guided Les Rouges to the 2024 Copa America semis, promoted overlooked players, and expanded the roster via dual-nationals. Under contract through this summer's World Cup, with contract extension discussions already underway.
Tactics till May 2026
Canada press with intensity from the front, built around a disciplined mid-block that transitions quickly. Crepeau starts in goal behind a back four of Johnston, Bombito, Cornelius and Laryea. Eustaquio and Kone form the midfield spine — the former organising and distributing, the latter providing the physical edge — while Davies and Buchanan offer constant danger as wide options. Jonathan David leads the attack, though whether he functions best as a traditional striker or a deeper false nine remains an open question. The team's tendency to run directly at opponents rather than building through phases is an acknowledged weakness Marsch has been working to correct.

Pedro "Bubista" Brito
56 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2020
Pedro Leitao Brito played for Cape Verde when their only international participation was the regional Amilcar Cabral Cup, going on to captain the country until 2005. He spent six years coaching in the Spanish lower leagues and six at Angolan club AS Aviacao. He served as assistant to national team coaches Joao de Deus and Lucio Antunes before replacing Rui Aguas in 2020, and was named CAF Coach of the Year for 2025.
Tactics till May 2026
Cape Verde play a strict 4-2-3-1 built around possession, direct wing play and quick passing through the middle of the park. Vozinha starts in goal behind S. Cabral, L. Costa, Diney and Joao Paulo, with Y. Semedo and K. Pina screening in midfield. Monteiro, the most experienced central midfielder in the squad, orchestrates play, looking for quick balls to striker Livramento as the wingers stay wide. Arcanjo and W. Semedo provide the attacking width. Long-range shooting has been a consistent feature in recent tournaments. The defensive line can be slow and easily exploited, and the gap between the most and least talented players in the squad is significant — collective spirit and motivation are as important as any tactical system.

Nestor Lorenzo
60 Yrs  ·  Since Jul 2022
Lorenzo shadowed Jose Pekerman for over a decade as his assistant, first with Argentina Under-20s and then Colombia between 2012 and 2018, before taking the hot seat at Peruvian side Melgar. The Boca Juniors fan led Melgar to the Copa Sudamericana quarter-finals, an achievement that likely wouldn't have earned a call from Colombia had it not been for his Pekerman connection. A former defender, he played in the 1990 World Cup final for Argentina before joining Swindon Town.
Tactics till May 2026
Colombia's shape is a 4-3-3 built around a high press and quick transitions, with James Rodriguez operating slightly deeper as the creative heartbeat and Luis Diaz the new primary figurehead, playing up top and drifting left. Vargas starts in goal behind Munoz, Sanchez, Lucumi and Mojica, with Rios and Lerma anchoring midfield, James ahead of them, J. Arias and Diaz wide, and Suarez leading the line. The three-man midfield balances defensive solidity with attacking purpose, though the full-backs' attacking instincts can leave the defence exposed wide. Getting Luis Suarez to perform the collaborative No.9 role Lorenzo prefers is the key selection challenge.

Zlatko Dalic
59 Yrs  ·  Since Oct 2017
Dalic is the longest-serving coach in Croatian national team history, leading the country to four major tournaments plus the 2023 UEFA Nations League final — one of the most significant national figures since independence. After a modest playing career he achieved coaching success with Al Hilal and Al Ain. His contract expires after the World Cup but the Croatian FA's full backing makes an extension to Euro 2028 likely.
Tactics till May 2026
Croatia's primary shape is a back three with Livakovic in goal behind Sutalo, Vuskovic and Caleta-Car, Stanisic and Gvardiol as wing-backs, Modric and Kovacic in central midfield, Perisic wide, and Kramaric and Budimir leading the attack. Dalic deployed a 4-2-3-1 for most of qualifying but switched to the back three to accommodate Vuskovic, and that is now the go-to formation. A reversion to 4-2-3-1 remains possible to add midfield bodies. Two trouble spots: a knee injury to Vuskovic suffered in April, and the left wing-back position, where Gvardiol's availability and preferred position create multiple selection permutations.

Fred Rutten
63 Yrs  ·  Since Feb 2026
Dutch coach who favours fast, balanced, workmanlike football built from the back. This is his first national team job, taking over from Dick Advocaat, whose tactical foundations he is not expected to change significantly. The challenge is whether he can match Advocaat's personal charisma with the squad and replicate his instinct for in-game adjustments on the biggest stage.
Tactics till May 2026
Curacao used a 5-4-1 with a false nine in the first game of the final qualifying round, and this is the setup most likely carried into the tournament. Room starts in goal behind a back five of Floranus, Obispo, Bazoer, Van Eijma and Sambo, with L. Bacuna, Comenencia and Hansen across the middle and Gorre as the lone forward. Bazoer, an Ajax academy graduate, is equally comfortable in central midfield and likely to be influential in both phases. Against stronger opponents, the plan is to sit deep, stay compact and exploit the pace of Gorre, Margaritha and Hansen on the counter, hoping for the opposition to make errors. The absence of a natural striker is the clearest structural question mark.

Miroslav Koubek
74 Yrs  ·  Since Dec 2025
Koubek, set to be the World Cup's oldest-ever coach, pairs a grandfatherly manner with a sharp tactical mind. His greatest successes came later in life, guiding Banik Ostrava and Viktoria Plzen to Czech league titles. He was named 2024 Czech Coach of the Year. His weapon is collective team spirit over individual brilliance.
Tactics till May 2026
Koubek cuts his tactical cloth according to the opponent, making line-ups hard to predict. The primary shape is a back three/back five. Krejci and Hranac are likely starters, with Chaloupek or Holes competing for the third centre-back spot. Coufal is a fixture at right wing-back. In midfield, Soucek and Darida are the veterans, though their partnership remains unsettled. Schick is the lone striker, supported by Sulc, with Chory and Chytil providing height and power off the bench.

Sebastien Desabre
49 Yrs  ·  Since Aug 2022
Desabre has garnered extensive praise for his work with DR Congo, evolving his reputation after a journeyman career on the continent. In his mid-30s he got a post at ASEC Abidjan before a steady procession of club jobs in Cameroon, Tunisia, Angola, the UAE, Algeria, Morocco and Egypt, and being appointed Uganda coach in 2017. In 2022 he was named DR Congo coach, taking them to the 2023 AFCON semi-finals and the last 16 in Morocco.
Tactics till May 2026
DR Congo employ a high press and look to dominate possession, with the X-factor being the probing play of Wissa and either Bongonda or Elia on the right, and Bakambu leading the attacking line. Mpasi starts in goal behind Wan-Bissaka, Mbemba, Tuanzebe and Masuaku, with Sadiki and Moutoussamy in central midfield and Mbuku providing width. Wan-Bissaka's arrival has markedly improved defensive discipline while also adding attacking threat down the right. The team's cohesion — built by converting diaspora players into committed Congolese representatives — is as important as any tactical system, and further recruitment before the tournament is possible.

Sebastian Beccacece
45 Yrs  ·  Since Aug 2024
A youthful-looking Argentine who never played professionally, Beccacece built his reputation as a restless, intense assistant to Jorge Sampaoli across clubs in Peru, Chile and Ecuador, helping Chile win their first Copa America in 2015. He later managed clubs in Argentina and Spain before taking charge of Ecuador, bringing both national team experience and direct knowledge of the country.
Tactics till May 2026
Ecuador's base formation is a 4-4-1-1, with the flexibility to shift into a 4-4-2, 4-3-3, 4-5-1 or 3-4-3 without major disruption. Galindez starts in goal behind Hincapie, Pacho, Ordonez and Franco, with midfielder Franco deployed at right-back to add a presence in central areas, Ordonez covering space behind him. Yeboah and Caicedo anchor the midfield, with Vite, Angulo and Plata ahead of them and Enner Valencia as the veteran striker. The most pressing concern is Caicedo's suspension for the opening match — his ability to burst forward is central to how Ecuador create, and he has no obvious replacement. More broadly, finding consistent goal-scoring support for Valencia remains the unresolved question running through the entire campaign.

Hossam Hassan
59 Yrs  ·  Since Feb 2024
Egypt's lead striker at the 1990 World Cup, Hassan set a then-world record of 177 caps across an extraordinary 21-year international career, scoring 69 goals. His coaching record has been far less impressive, with a temperamental streak and frequent outbursts landing him in trouble. He had a brief spell with Jordan in 2013. His twin brother Ibrahim is one of his assistants.
Tactics till May 2026
Egypt's default approach is a low defensive block, sitting deep and looking to counter on the pace of Trezeguet, Marmoush and Salah. For the opening game against Belgium they are likely to start with five across the back, with M. El Shenawy in goal behind Hany, Ibrahim, Abdelmaguid, Kanaanizadegan and Khalilzadeh. Ezatolahi and Attia screen in midfield, with Ashour, H. Fathy and Rabia ahead of them and Salah, Marmoush and Fatouh as the attacking outlets. For the later group games a more expansive 4-2-3-1, which yielded a 0-0 draw with Spain and a 4-0 win over Saudi Arabia in March, may be used instead. Maintaining any kind of possession game has been an acknowledged weakness.

Thomas Tuchel
52 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2025
Tuchel has scarcely put a foot wrong since becoming England head coach. England players like him for his reputation as a dynamic, trophy-winning manager, his enthusiasm and individuality. He is also enjoying life in London, which partly explains his willingness to extend his contract to 2028 when approached by the FA.
Tactics till May 2026
England's settled system is a 4-2-3-1, with Pickford in goal behind James, Konsa, Guehi and O'Reilly, Anderson and Rice in central midfield, Bellingham or Rogers at ten, Saka and Gordon wide, and Kane as the focal point. High-intensity pressing is Tuchel's hallmark, though this carries risk in high-temperature venues. Set pieces are a notable weapon, with Rice and Saka delivering from corners. Bench depth is considered one of England's key advantages going into the tournament.

Didier Deschamps
57 Yrs  ·  Since Jul 2012
Deschamps is one of the most successful international coaches of the century, having already secured legendary status captaining Les Bleus to the 1998 World Cup on home soil. He had moderate club success, leading Monaco to the 2004 Champions League final and Marseille to the Ligue 1 title in 2010. He has since led France to two World Cup finals, winning one, making him the standard-bearer of international management.
Tactics till May 2026
France's expected shape places Maignan behind a back four of Digne, Upamecano, Saliba and Kounde, with Tchouameni and Kone in midfield, Olise at ten, and Mbappe, Barcola and Dembele ahead — a structured 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3. The key tactical problem is the absence of players occupying central zones — Mbappe's free-roam role creates gaps in build-up and finishing. At Euro 2024, no France player scored from open play until the semi-final defeat. Fitting together the attacking talent without sacrificing defensive solidity is Deschamps' central unsolved challenge.

Julian Nagelsmann
38 Yrs  ·  Since Sep 2023
The second-youngest Bundestrainer of all time, Nagelsmann is an intelligent, progressive thinker — bold enough to declare the world title the only acceptable goal. Sacked by Bayern in spring 2023 in a dismissal widely considered undeserved, he was appointed that September. His first tournament, Euro 2024 on home soil, ended in a narrow quarter-final extra-time defeat to Spain.
Tactics till May 2026
Nagelsmann sets up primarily in a 4-2-3-1, with a high press, pro-active approach and a great deal of fluidity between the lines. Baumann starts in goal behind Raum, Schlotterbeck, Tah and Kimmich, the captain whose driving runs inside from right-back are central to how the team builds. Goretzka and Pavlovic screen in front of them, with Sane, Musiala and Wirtz — interchangeable and technically outstanding — operating across the attacking midfield band behind Havertz. Almost a third of their qualification goals came from set pieces, a reminder of their threat at dead balls. No unresolved positions are flagged.

Carlos Queiroz
73 Yrs  ·  Since Apr 2026
Queiroz declared his Ghana appointment a mission rather than just another job. The Portuguese has had a decent career at club level, winning silverware with Real Madrid and Sporting, but has yet to fully distinguish himself at international level. Whether at South Africa, Portugal, Iran, Colombia, Egypt, Oman, the UAE or Qatar, his career as a national team coach has been more of what could have been. The Ghana role gives him a unique opportunity to finally silence his doubters.
Tactics till May 2026
Ghana's shape places Asare in goal behind Lamptey, Peprah Oppong, Djiku and Kohn, with Yirenkyi and Partey in central midfield, Williams and Kudus wide, and Semenyo and J. Ayew leading the attack. The midfield is the central puzzle — Ghana have been thin in this area for years, and finding the best partner for Partey is Queiroz's biggest challenge. Yirenkyi, a 20-year-old all-action midfielder previously misused at right-back, is the leading candidate. The goalkeeping position is also genuinely unsettled, with Asare the current No.1 but former starter Ati-Zigi still considered by many to be Ghana's best keeper.

Sebastien Migne
53 Yrs  ·  Since Mar 2024
A journeyman French coach who was assistant to Rigobert Song when Cameroon shocked Brazil at the 2022 World Cup. Appointed to Haiti mid-instability, he has yet to visit the island but earned local goodwill by recruiting diaspora talent including Bellegarde and Isidor. Three good results at this tournament could firmly establish his reputation.
Tactics till May 2026
Haiti favour a 4-2-3-1 that can blur into a 4-2-4, with Migne occasionally starting two strikers. Placide plays in goal behind a back four of Arcus, Ade, Delcroix and Lacroix, with Leverton Pierre and Casimir tasked with providing cover in front of them. Bellegarde is the creative hub, given an attack-minded supporting cast of wingers and Providence in behind Wilson Isidor, the preferred No.9, with Duckens and Pierrot as alternatives. The defensive frailty is a real concern — Haiti conceded three or more goals in a quarter of their 2025 outings — and the two midfielders will have enormous ground to cover protecting a back line that sits behind a very adventurous front four.

Amir Ghalenoei
62 Yrs  ·  Since Mar 2023
An old-fashioned but successful domestic manager with five Iranian league titles, though the last came in 2013. This is his second stint with the national team — the first ended in failure at the 2007 Asian Cup. Reappointed despite lingering scepticism among fans, he has yet to convert many critics. Progressing from the group would go a long way to changing that.
Tactics till May 2026
Iran are expected to use a compact defensive mid-block, pressing opponents in the spaces between the lines, winning the ball back and launching fluid counter-attacks — an approach ingrained over a decade under previous coaches Queiroz and Skocic. Beiranvand starts in goal behind Hardani, Kanaanizadegan, Khalilzadeh and Mohammadi, with Mo. Mohebi and Ezatolahi in central midfield. Ghoddos operates in the band ahead of them, with Ghayedi and Azmoun as wide threats and Taremi as the primary striker. Set pieces are a significant weapon given the squad's exceptional height. Maintaining defensive solidity — a persistent problem in qualifying — is the central challenge, and with the Iranian league halted due to the war, the disruption to preparation looms large.

Graham Arnold
62 Yrs  ·  Since May 2025
Arnold is a grizzled veteran of Asian football who prides himself on motivation and extracting the best from his players. He stepped down as Australia manager in September 2024 after six years in his second spell, before arriving in Baghdad eight months later. His ability to connect with supporters has endeared him to Iraqi fans, who recognise his passion for the role. Hero status, the article notes, is well within reach.
Tactics till May 2026
Iraq defend from the front with two strikers closing down the opposition, built around target man Aymen Hussein holding the ball up to bring midfielders into play, with a more mobile forward alongside him to run in behind. Hassan starts in goal behind H. Ali, Tahseen, Iqbal and Amyn, with Al Ammari and Hashim in central midfield, Jasim and Doski ahead, and Hussein and M. Ali leading the line. Ali Jasim gives Iraq more technical control in possession. Wide men are expected to contribute defensively as well as offensively. Discipline is a noted weakness — red cards have been a recurring issue, and managing the team's tendency to get overexcited in big moments is Arnold's priority.

Emerse Fae
42 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2024
A 41-cap ex-international who featured in the 2006 World Cup squad, Fae had no prior senior coaching experience before being promoted from assistant when Jean-Louis Gasset left during the 2023 AFCON finals, with Ivory Coast barely through the group stage. They went on to win the tournament, and he has held the post ever since.
Tactics till May 2026
Ivory Coast's shape features Doue in goal behind Konan, Ndicka and Kossounou, with Y. Fofana and I. Sangare as the defensive midfield base and Kessie and Inao Oulai in the central band ahead of them. Amad Diallo, now firmly the team's talisman, and teenager Yan Diomande operate as the attacking outlets, with Guessand leading the line. The full-backs push high to maximise width, and speed is the team's primary weapon. The concern is a tendency toward rigidity and over-reliance on individual brilliance — if Amad or Inao Oulai are not at their best, the attack becomes blunt. The No.9 position is also unresolved, with Haller's fitness uncertain, Guessand filling in and Wahi in contention after switching international allegiance.

Hajime Moriyasu
57 Yrs  ·  Since Jul 2018
A former defensive midfielder who narrowly missed Japan's USA '94 squad, Moriyasu won three titles with his former club Sanfrecce Hiroshima before serving as assistant to Akira Nishino at the 2018 World Cup. Taking over after Russia 2018, he led Japan at the Tokyo Olympics and in Qatar. November's 3-0 win over Bolivia was his 100th match in charge. Known as a team leader who listens and delegates well, he is Japan's longest-serving manager.
Tactics till May 2026
Japan's first-choice formation is a back three — the system that proved decisive against Germany and Spain in Qatar — with Z. Suzuki in goal behind Taniguchi, Watanabe and H. Ito. Doan and Endo cover the midfield ahead of them, with Ka. Sano and Nakamura providing width and Mitoma, Kubo and Ueda as the attacking trident. High pressing, fast ball movement and dynamic use of the full width of the pitch define the approach. When under pressure they can drop into a patient compact shape, and their capacity for mid-game tactical switches — including a shift to a back four — is well established. Captain Endo's fitness is a concern after racing to be ready for the tournament.

Jamal Sellami
55 Yrs  ·  Since Jun 2024
There was little fanfare when Sellami was appointed in 2024, another Moroccan following the popular Hussein Ammouta. All of his experience had come in his home country, including leading Morocco's A team to victory in the 2018 African Nations Championship. He has continued Jordan's rise with minimum fuss, building real togetherness throughout the ranks, with attention to detail and organisational skills that have produced an improved team spirit and ability to get results under pressure.
Tactics till May 2026
Jordan sit deep and counter-attack, with the precise attacking shape dependent on whether injured target man Yazan Al Naimat is fit — if so, he partners Ali Olwan centrally, with Mahmoud Al Mardi wide; if not, Olwan leads the line. Abulaila starts in goal behind Haddad, Al Rashdan, Jamous and Nasib, with Al Arab and Abualnadi in central midfield, Abu Taha and Al Tamari providing width. Both wing-backs can advance quickly, and getting the ball into the box is central to the approach. Al Tamari is the key creative threat. Jordan are comfortable being unfancied and have shown the mental strength to produce results when pressure is highest.

Javier Aguirre
67 Yrs  ·  Since Jul 2024
Aguirre is arguably Mexico's best-ever manager — reliable and pragmatic rather than spectacular. Mostly built in Spain and with El Tri, his strength lies in organising and steadying the ship. In his third stint, he has restored competitiveness, though whether he can elevate this limited generation remains to be seen. Long-term, Rafael Marquez is set to replace him.
Tactics till May 2026
Aguirre has primarily used a 4–3–3, but has experimented with a 3–4–2–1 that better suits his squad. He is likely to keep switching formations even during the tournament. The goalkeeper spot remains a trouble area — Malagon lost his place through errors, Rangel lacks confidence, and veteran Ochoa (40) may be the best option. In defence, Vasquez, Montes and Gallardo are settled starters. Jimenez leads the attack, but his supporting cast is undecided, and wonderkid Mora may only feature as a substitute.

Mohamed Ouahbi
49 Yrs  ·  Since Mar 2026
Belgian-born of Moroccan parentage, Ouahbi started as a part-time teacher-coach before rising through Anderlecht's youth ranks to assistant of the first team. Appointed Morocco Under-20 coach in 2022, he won the Under-20 World Cup in Chile, beating Argentina in the final. Promoted to replace Regragui mid-cycle, he arrives with momentum but minimal senior experience.
Tactics till May 2026
Morocco operate in a compact 4-1-4-1 or 4-3-3 that shifts into a 4-4-2 defensive block, conceding just twice in eight World Cup qualifiers. Under previous coach Regragui the approach was deeply conservative, but Ouahbi moved toward more possession and faster penetration at the recent AFCON. Bounou starts in goal, with Hakimi, Aguerd, Masina and Mazraoui forming the back four and El Aynaoui sitting in front of them. Ezzalzouli, Saibari, El Khannouss and Brahim operate in the attacking band behind En-Nesyri. A significant concern is the Champions League semi-final injury Hakimi is carrying, which threatens to disrupt the entire attacking structure Morocco build around him.

Ronald Koeman
63 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2023
Part of the Euro '88-winning side — the only Dutch team to have won a trophy — Koeman is now in his second spell in charge after leaving in 2020 for Barcelona. As a coach he prefers results over beauty, is not afraid to criticise his players openly, and restored national pride with a Nations League final and a semi-final at Euro 2024. This may be his last tournament, and the decision on his future will be made after the finals.
Tactics till May 2026
Koeman's pragmatic approach means the traditional 4-3-3 remains most likely but could be exchanged for a 3-2-4-1 or 5-2-3 depending on the opponent. Roefs starts in goal, with Dumfries at right-back, Van Dijk as captain alongside J. Timber in central defence, and Van de Ven at the problematic left-back spot — though both he and Ake remain in contention at centre-back. Reijnders and De Jong partner in midfield, but lack a natural ball-winner, with Gravenberch or Quinten Timber the likeliest solutions. Memphis Depay is the undisputed No.9, with Gakpo, Kluivert and Malen competing for the spot alongside him following Xavi Simons' serious knee injury.

Darren Bazeley
53 Yrs  ·  Since Mar 2023
An ex-Watford, Wolves and Walsall defender who made his name in age-group coaching but remains relatively unproven at senior level. He was seen as a safe pair of hands when appointed three years ago as higher-profile candidates fell away, and is popular with the squad for his player-driven approach. Affable and likeable, he will need a ruthless edge at the tournament.
Tactics till May 2026
New Zealand's primary formation is a 4-2-3-1, occasionally shifting to a more defensive 4-3-3. Paulsen and Crocombe are competing for the goalkeeper spot, with Payne, Boxall, Surman and Cacace forming the back four — though Payne has been sidelined for much of the season, leaving raw alternative Callan Elliott as cover. Stamenic and Bell anchor the midfield, with Thomas, Just and Randall ahead of them and Wood leading the line. The team favours a possession-based game, though Bazeley has called for more directness and variety. Wood is almost impossible to replace and can be isolated without a second striker, Sarpreet Singh is the creative No.10 but is injury-prone, and the lack of natural wingers — with full-backs routinely providing width — remains the clearest structural vulnerability.

Stale Solbakken
58 Yrs  ·  Since Dec 2020
Solbakken had his playing career cut short by a heart attack on the training ground at FC Copenhagen, an experience he later said helped him understand what truly matters. He took charge of Norway in 2020 after successful spells managing FC Copenhagen, but came under sustained criticism when the team failed to qualify for the 2022 World Cup and Euro 2024. He signed a new deal in December 2025 following Norway's successful qualifying campaign.
Tactics till May 2026
Norway's primary shape is a 4-2/4-3-3 hybrid, dropping into a 4-4-2 out of possession with Odegaard and Haaland leading the press. Nyland starts in goal behind Ryerson, Ajer, Heggem and Moller Wolfe, with Berge and Aursnes alongside Odegaard in midfield and Nusa, Haaland and Sorloth in attack. In possession Sorloth joins Haaland in the box while Ryerson pushes high on the right. Nusa holds his left-wing place ahead of Schjelderup. Trouble spots include Moller Wolfe and Nyland's limited club game time, with keeper Haikin — Norwegian citizen after a fine Champions League season — pushing hard for the starting spot.

Thomas Christiansen
53 Yrs  ·  Since Jul 2020
Christiansen has quietly become one of the most important figures in Panama's modern football history. Since taking charge, the Danish-born former Spain international has built a team that reflects his personality: organised, disciplined and rarely chaotic. His approach is pragmatic rather than ambitious, prioritising structure over flair, but it has given Panama a level of CONCACAF consistency they never had before. Whether those traits translate to the world stage remains to be seen.
Tactics till May 2026
Panama's primary shape is a 3-4-2-1, with a possible shift to a 5-4-1 against stronger opponents. Mosquera starts in goal behind Blackman, Harvey and Escobar, with Martinez and Davis as wing-backs, Godoy and Carrasquilla in central midfield, Andrade and Barcenas behind Waterman as the striker. The two central midfielders are the team's most important players — Godoy providing the muscle to win the ball, Carrasquilla the technique to distribute. Barcenas' return from injury adds a creative spark that was absent in the final qualifying round. The compact low block is the tactical identity, looking to exploit space in behind with pace on the counter.

Gustavo Alfaro
63 Yrs  ·  Since Aug 2024
A one-time midfielder whose unspectacular club career in Argentina gave little indication of his coaching talent, Alfaro proved better with smaller clubs before being called up at short notice to rescue Ecuador's Qatar 2022 qualification. After a brief spell with Costa Rica, he is doing an even better job with Paraguay — restoring confidence, rescuing the campaign, and becoming a national hero who has carried the country from despair to euphoria.
Tactics till May 2026
Paraguay defend with characteristic grit, built around a solid defensive unit anchored by centre-back partners Alderete and Gustavo Gomez, with Gill in goal and Caceres at right back. Cubas sits as the midfield anchor alongside Bobadilla, with Almiron providing the link to attack. The central tactical question is how to get the best from both Enciso and Diego Gomez simultaneously — fielding Enciso wide on the right gives him freedom but questions his pace from the flank, while pushing Gomez deep frees space for another winger such as Sosa but takes him further from goal. Sanabria leads the line.

Roberto Martinez
52 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2023
Martinez was a surprise appointment who won over supporters with his natural charm and impressive displays during Euro 2024 qualifying. A mediocre showing at the tournament itself and some unexpected hiccups during World Cup qualifying have eroded support for the Spaniard, despite the UEFA Nations League victory in 2025. His tactical flexibility has largely been beneficial, though a tendency to overthink has led to questionable line-ups. This is likely his last tournament at the helm.
Tactics till May 2026
Portugal utilise 4-3-3, 4-2-3-1 and 3-4-3 formations depending on the opponent, always built around possession dominance and control rather than transition. D. Costa starts in goal behind Cancelo, Dias, Inacio and Mendes, with J. Neves and Vitinha in central midfield, B. Fernandes ahead of them, and Leao, Ronaldo and Neto in attack. Full-backs advance and cut inside to create final-third overloads, with the technically gifted midfield as the engine. Against deep, packed backlines Portugal can struggle to break through. Whether Ronaldo starts alongside Goncalo Ramos early in the tournament is the key selection question.

Julen Lopetegui
59 Yrs  ·  Since May 2025
Lopetegui is a well-travelled Spaniard whose possession-based style cost him at Bernabeu, Sevilla, Wolverhampton and West Ham. Now coaching Qatar, his first World Cup match as manager, he must show greater adaptability after his preferred style proved ill-suited to lower-table Premier League football. Qatar represent a fresh opportunity to finally deliver at a major tournament.
Tactics till May 2026
Qatar line up in a 4-2-3-1 that moves to a back three in possession, with the full-back on Afif's side pushing forward to free him from wide areas. Barsham starts in goal behind Miguel, Khouki, Mendes and Al Brake, with Madibo and Boudiaf sitting as the midfield pivot. The entire system is designed to get the best from Afif, the two-time Asian Footballer of the Year, who roams freely across the pitch. Al Mannai and Edmilson Junior provide width, with Almoez Ali leading the line. Almost every other starting position beyond Afif remains genuinely unsettled, and Lopetegui has yet to find a stable lineup despite experimenting throughout the Arab Cup and subsequent friendlies.

Giorgios Donis
56 Yrs  ·  Since Apr 2026
A former Greece international whose playing career at Panathinaikos, Blackburn Rovers and Huddersfield Town gave little indication of what followed. It was his time coaching in the Saudi Pro League with four different clubs that caught the federation's eye. He left Al Khaleej to take over the Green Falcons in late April — the appointment was sudden, and adapting quickly is a necessity.
Tactics till May 2026
Donis favours a 4-2-3-1 system, though he has shown flexibility with 4-4-2 and 5-3-2 alternatives. Al Aqidi starts in goal behind Abdulhamid, Al Tambakti, Kadesh and Boushal, with Kanno and N. Al Dawsari sitting as the midfield screen. Al Juwayr and S. Al Dawsari provide the creative threat, with Al Oboud behind Al Buraikan as striker. The creative burden has fallen heavily on an ageing Salem Al Dawsari, and while the emergence of Al Juwayr is welcome, it is a lot to ask of a young player. With strikers out of form at club level, the likely approach is defensive solidity first, with counter-attacks and set pieces as the primary route to goal.

Steve Clarke
62 Yrs  ·  Since May 2019
Clarke began as an assistant to Mourinho and Dalglish before becoming manager at West Brom. It was his work at Kilmarnock, turning a struggling side into European qualifiers, that caught the SFA's eye. Now in his seventh year and third major tournament following Euros in 2021 and 2024, he has transformed Scotland from perennial strugglers to regular qualifiers, becoming the first manager since Craig Brown to guide them to a World Cup.
Tactics till May 2026
Scotland set up in a 4-2-3-1 built around their midfield strength, with Gordon in goal behind Tierney, Hanley, McKenna and Robertson. Ferguson and Christie sit as the double pivot, with McGinn pushed forward into a No.10 role and Robertson providing overlapping width on the left. Gannon-Doak is the exciting option on the right, though his fitness is a concern after going off injured against Denmark. Dykes leads the line for his physicality, with Adams and Shankland offering different qualities in reserve. The absence of a top-class centre-forward is a persistent weakness, and with Gilmour having missed qualifiers through injury, the midfield depth Clarke can call upon remains uncertain.

Pape Thiaw
45 Yrs  ·  Since Dec 2024
Thiaw was in the squad that reached the 2002 World Cup quarter-finals, playing only once. He coached Senegal's home-based players to success in the 2022 African Nations Championship before taking over the senior team from Aliou Cisse. His route to the role was controversial — a fine and five-match ban followed scenes at the AFCON final — though the ban only takes effect when the next AFCON qualifiers begin in September.
Tactics till May 2026
Senegal's approach is physical and direct, built around speed of movement, midfield overloads and quick transitions down the flanks using Mane, Sarr, Ibrahim Mbaye and Iliman Ndiaye. E. Mendy starts in goal behind Diatta, Koulibaly, Niakhate and E. Diouf, with Gana Gueye and Diarra in central midfield and Pape Gueye driving forward, alongside I. Sarr and Jackson in attack. The centre-back partnership is unsettled — Koulibaly's errors at AFCON are a concern, though he offers leadership. The No.9 position is the biggest headache, with Jackson too inconsistent and Dia and Habib Diallo having failed to take their chances.

Hugo Broos
74 Yrs  ·  Since May 2021
Broos ends his career as he hoped, with a World Cup appearance as coach. Spending five years at the helm, he will become South Africa's longest-serving coach. He took them to third at the 2023 AFCON finals and won two Belgian championships with Club Brugge and one with Anderlecht. He retires after the finals.
Tactics till May 2026
South Africa play a high-tempo transition game, primarily using pace and width. Wingers Appollis and Mofokeng offer acceleration and trickery, with Mudau effective on the right. Lyle Foster leads the line. Mokoena is the midfield fixture, though finding a playmaker remains a trouble spot since Themba Zwane's knee injury has kept him sidelined for 18 months. Broos is gambling on the 36-year-old being fit in time.

Hong Myung-bo
57 Yrs  ·  Since Jul 2024
Hong captained Korea at four World Cups before moving into coaching. His tenure has lacked consistency and a clear identity, with frequent personnel and formation changes. Not a popular reappointment, the challenge is whether he can give the team's stars the platform to perform without over-relying on big names. His coaching reputation will be decided in Mexico.
Tactics till May 2026
Hong has experimented with a back three and back four, with a back four now likely the preferred option. The team likes to move forward quickly using pace. Hwang In-beom sets the tempo in central midfield, with Jens Castrop alongside him, though Castrop could also fill in at full-back. Son Heung-min is the star, deployed centrally or wide. Oh Hyeon-gyu and Cho Gue-sung provide striking options. Trouble spots include injuries to Hwang, Won Du-jae and Park Yong-woo, plus unresolved full-back positions.

Luis De La Fuente
64 Yrs  ·  Since Dec 2022
A former Athletic Club Bilbao full-back from Haro in Rioja, De La Fuente was largely unknown when appointed, his only first-team experience an uninspiring 11-game spell with third-tier Alaves. But he had won the Euros at Under-19 and Under-21 level and, promoted from within the federation, went on to lead Spain to the senior Euros title and the UEFA Nations League.
Tactics till May 2026
Spain's primary shape is a 4-2-3-1 that can look like a 4-3-3 depending on personnel, with Pedri now playing deeper. Simon starts in goal behind Cucurella, Laporte, Cubarsi and Llorente, with Rodri and Fabian as the midfield base and Pedri ahead of them. Williams and Yamal provide width, with Oyarzabal as the forward. Full-backs are encouraged to push high while centre-backs play out from the back. Several positions are unsettled — Nico Williams' fitness opens the door for Victor Munoz or an inverted option on the left, Fabian Ruiz is carrying a knee issue, Merino is racing to be fit, and whether there is room for both Rodri and Zubimendi simultaneously remains an open question.

Graham Potter
50 Yrs  ·  Since Oct 2025
An English coach who began his managerial career at Ostersunds FK in the fourth tier of Swedish football, winning successive promotions and the domestic cup before moving to Brighton, where he had real success, and then struggling at Chelsea and West Ham. A return to Sweden proved the natural fit — his understanding of Swedish football and command of the language make him highly respected in his adopted home.
Tactics till May 2026
Potter settled on a 3-4-3 by the play-offs after initially using a 4-4-2. The back three is expected to be Isak, Lagerbielke and Lindelof, with Gudmundsson at left wing-back and Holm — returning from a calf injury — at right. Ayari and Karlstrom, who acquitted themselves well in the play-offs, start in central midfield. Elanga provides pace and width, Gyokeres is an automatic starter as the talismanic centre-forward. The central unresolved question is whether a fit Alexander Isak can coexist in the same starting XI as Gyokeres, and if so, what the balanced tactical solution looks like. Kulusevski's absence means Nygren is the current alternative in the creative attacking role.

Murat Yakin
51 Yrs  ·  Since Aug 2021
Basel-raised Yakin arrived as a surprise appointment managing in the Swiss second tier. His reign hit a low with a 6-1 loss to Portugal, but a strong Euro 2024 — including a back-three switch that took Switzerland to the quarter-finals — restored his standing. Now in a third consecutive qualification, his easy-going manner and tactical shrewdness have made him popular. His future beyond this tournament is unmentioned.
Tactics till May 2026
Switzerland operate in a 4-2-3-1 with a settled defensive foundation, Yakin having moved back to a four-man backline after experimenting with a back three at Euro 2024, though a 3-4-3 was deployed against Norway in March. Kobel starts in goal behind Widmer, Elvedi, Akanji and Rodriguez, with Xhaka and Freuler providing the double pivot. Rieder has most often filled the No.10 role behind lone striker Embolo, though his inconsistency keeps the position open, with Sow, Manzambi, Amdouni and Sanches all in contention. Amdouni and Sanches are both returning from injury, adding further uncertainty to the one position that could determine how much Switzerland's considerable attacking talent is unlocked.

Sabri Lamouchi
54 Yrs  ·  Since Jan 2026
A French international midfielder of Tunisian parentage who made 12 appearances for Les Bleus and was part of the 1998 World Cup squad. After a playing career spanning Internazionale and Marseille among others, he was a surprise appointment to coach Ivory Coast with no prior experience, qualifying them for the 2014 World Cup before quitting after the group stage. Subsequent spells at Rennes, Nottingham Forest and Cardiff City all proved brief.
Tactics till May 2026
Tunisia's approach is built on defensive solidity, with tall centre-backs and robust full-backs making them difficult to break down. Dahmen starts in goal behind Valery, Bronn, Talbi and Abdi, though the goalkeeping position is genuinely unsettled — experienced options Bechir Ben Said and Aymen Dahmen were passed over in March, and Noureddine Farhat cannot be ruled out either. Skhiri conducts from midfield with Khedira alongside him, while Hannibal Mejbri and Ismael Gharbi interchange in the advanced role ahead of them. Achouri operates on the right wing with Tounekti or Saad on the left. The No.9 position is an acknowledged weak spot — Ben Farhat is highly regarded but teenage, with Chaouat and Elloumi as more natural options. With limited time working with the squad, Lamouchi's tactical approach remains an open question.

Vincenzo Montella
51 Yrs  ·  Since Sep 2023
No Turkey manager since the turn of the century holds a better points-per-game average in competitive fixtures than Montella's 2.16, surpassing even Senol Gunes and Fatih Terim. The first foreign boss to qualify Turkey for both a Euros and a World Cup, he also steered the side into the top tier of the UEFA Nations League in 2024-25. His success has put him firmly on Italy's radar as a future Azzurri coach.
Tactics till May 2026
Turkey's primary formation is a 4-2-3-1 built on meticulous organisation, with a safety-first 5-4-1 used against stronger opponents — deployed to good effect in a qualifying draw in Spain. Cakir starts in goal behind Celik, Demiral, Bardakci and Kadioglu, the marauding left-back who is central to Turkey's attacking width. Calhanoglu sits deep as the midfield general controlling tempo, with Yuksek alongside him. Guler and Yildiz provide attacking brilliance in the final third, with Kokcu linking play and Akturkoglu leading the line despite being more naturally suited to a wide role — finding a genuine centre-forward solution remains the outstanding problem.

Mauricio Pochettino
54 Yrs  ·  Since Sep 2024
Argentine tactician whose record at Spurs in developing young players made him the standout candidate to lead the US at a home World Cup. US Soccer hope that same ability to help players reach their potential translates from club to international football. His meticulous approach and trusted team of assistants have quickly brought tactical cohesion to a squad with plenty of overseas experience but previously lacking a clear identity.
Tactics till May 2026
Pochettino's system adapts to personnel rather than imposing a fixed shape, with a 4-4-2 used defensively and pressing phases shifting into 4-2-3-1 or back-three formations in possession. Freese starts in goal behind Freeman, Richards, Ream and Robinson, with Adams and Tessmann providing the midfield base. Pulisic operates as the creative focal point, McKennie adds box-to-box energy, Weah offers width, and Balogun leads the attack. The fluidity of full-back positioning — centre-backs drifting wide, full-backs becoming wingers — is a deliberate feature rather than a vulnerability, though it demands high tactical intelligence from every outfield player.

Marcelo Bielsa
70 Yrs  ·  Since May 2023
Presumably drawing towards the end of a hugely influential career, Bielsa is a man who would freely admit he has won more admirers than titles. For well over 30 years his high-intensity attacking style was seen as revolutionary, but his ideas have now become mainstream and he has lost his edge. This is his third World Cup with his third South American side, after Argentina in 2002 and Chile in 2010.
Tactics till May 2026
Uruguay's standard formation is a 4-3-3 built around a high press and wide wingers aiming to get behind the opposition and create for the centre-forward, though a 4-2-4 has been used in desperation. Rochet starts in goal behind Varela, R. Araujo, Gimenez and Olivera, with Ugarte and Valverde in the midfield base and De Arrascaeta at the head of the triangle. Nunez, Canobbio and M. Araujo provide the attacking options. The central puzzle is De Arrascaeta — Uruguay have struggled to fit a conventional No.10 into a Bielsa system, but his form has forced the issue, obliging a choice between Ugarte and Bentancur alongside Valverde. Whether his presence limits Valverde's freedom to push higher is the unresolved tactical question running through the entire setup.

Fabio Cannavaro
52 Yrs  ·  Since Oct 2025
Cannavaro lifted the 2006 World Cup and is remembered as one of the great defenders, but his coaching career has not matched that legacy. He won the Chinese title with Guangzhou when the team were dominant and made little impact elsewhere. It was a gamble from Uzbekistan, who had more experienced options available, with the former Ballon d'Or winner given just a few months to prepare. His comments and work-rate, having been spotted at many stadiums watching games, have impressed.
Tactics till May 2026
Cannavaro's focus is on defensive discipline, concentration and hard work — the traditional characteristics of Italian football. Yusupov starts in goal behind Alijonov, Khusanov, Ashurmatov and Nasrullaev, with Shukurov and Hamrobekov in central midfield, Fayzullaev and Masharipov providing width and Urunov behind Shomurodov. The formation has been a back three or five in friendlies, with a flat back four possible for the tournament itself. Shomurodov is the attacking focal point but risks isolation. Defensive solidity has been solid until the latter stages — improving concentration levels late in games is Cannavaro's priority.
